transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Maya Ortiz (Cedar - Head of ML), Ben Liu (Cedar - Platform Eng), Sophie Chang (Cedar - Product), Jordan Park (Cedar - Security)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Action items captured.

00:00 Alex: okay um hi everyone thanks for joining from Redwood side Alex here, AE, and Priya our solutions engineer, Samir on CSM. um how's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya: good thanks, excited to see the console. we want to understand how you show per-route costs and how to track chat vs embeddings spending.
00:12 Ben: also network questions and data residency, and we need RBAC for internal teams.
00:18 Alex: perfect, brief agenda: quick qualification (stack + objectives), walkthrough of Console (usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown), quick look at Optimize recommendations, then Q&A and next steps.
03:05 Priya: jumping into the console now, i'm sharing my screen - you'll see the Home overview: total tokens, spend, and a delta vs previous period. quick note: the numbers are tokenized and normalized across models so we can show per-token unit cost even if you run different model variants.
04:00 Maya: is that normalized to a single token price across models? we run a mix of GPT-like and llama variants.
04:08 Priya: good question - we show both normalized tokens and canonical token costs per model. the per-route breakdown uses the model selected on that route to compute actual spend; we also surface an "adjusted cost" if you apply Optimize recommendations like switching quantized variant. sometimes the transcript shows "optimise" spelled odd in the UI export.
06:20 Alex: quick qualification - what are the top routes you care about? Maya: chat-widget (customer support), embeddings-search, and a rerank route for recommendations.
07:00 Alex: timeline? Sophie: aiming for a pilot in 2-3 weeks to validate cost/SLOs and then decide about Dedicated vs Hosted.
08:10 Priya: back to the dashboard - here's Per-Route Metrics. each route has its own card: requests per minute, p50/p95 latency, tokens in/out, fail rate, and cost column showing per-route spend for the selected window. you can segment by model version, region, and environment (prod/stage).
09:30 Ben: can we set spend alerts per route?
09:34 Priya: yes, alerting + quotas. you can set monthly caps per route and auto-fallback policies; eg if chat-widget exceeds cost threshold we can route to a lower-cost model or limit tokens.
11:00 Priya: showing a token-level breakdown view - this ties each API call (route invocation) to a token delta and approximate cost, aggregated. note transcription: sometimes caller names get fudged in the export.
12:20 Maya: how granular is the cost data - near real-time?
12:27 Priya: near real-time for usage; full reconciliation (billing-ready) is within 24 hours. console shows estimated spend in realtime and final reconciled numbers later.
14:05 Alex: switching to the Cost Explorer - you can slice by route, by model, by tag (we support arbitrary route tags) and by team. this is how platform teams get per-product allocations.
15:30 Maya: do you support chargeback to our internal cost centers?
15:34 Alex: yes - exportable CSVs and an integration with FinOps tooling; also you can map routes to cost centers and download monthly chargeback reports.
17:00 Priya: demoing per-route drilldown for chat-widget - here's the timeline of requests, cost spikes aligned with long context windows, and suggestions from Optimize: reduce sequence length for system prompts, enable KV cache on recurrent sessions, and consider a quantized variant for lower-cost bursts.
18:44 Ben: what's KV cache?
18:48 Priya: sorry k-v cache, it's our prefix caching for repeated context in chat - saves tokens and latency by caching cached key-value cache entries so you don't resend full context each time. some transcriptions in exports flip K-V to KV or K V, so keep an eye.
20:30 Maya: we're regulated - audit logs and SSO are must-haves.
20:33 Alex: absolutely - console has audit trails for each API key and route change, full admin RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC), and support for customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
22:10 Jordan (Security): do you store PII in logs? what's retention?
22:18 Priya: by default logs are redacted for user input, and you can configure retention windows; for Private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC and bring your own KMS.
24:00 Alex: now pan to the per-route cost breakdown example - chat-widget consumed 46% of tokens but 62% of spend because it uses the larger model. embeddings route is high volume but low per-token cost. we also surface per-token unit cost and the estimated dollars per 1M tokens for each model.
26:30 Sophie: can we see historical model switch impact? like before/after quantization?
26:35 Priya: yes, use the Compare view - pick time ranges and model variants; Optimize will simulate cost delta and quality risk based on your evals. sometimes the explanation text says "quality regressions" and we tie that to your prompt set.
29:10 Alex: quick demo of Optimize recommendations - shows batching suggestions, quantified latency vs cost tradeoffs, and per-route recommended batch size. you can apply recommendations to a route or test in a canary.
31:00 Ben: for production we may want Dedicated - how does the console differ for Dedicated customers?
31:06 Alex: Dedicated customers get a tenant view with capacity metrics, reserved throughput, and a slightly different cost model. console still shows per-route dashboards and per-token attribution; bills are reconciled to committed capacity.
33:15 Maya: regarding SLOs, can we set p95 latency targets per route and get automatic fallback?
33:22 Priya: yes, set target SLOs per route and a policy such as fallback to a cheaper model or spill to a different region. console will show SLO heatmaps and alert when projections exceed thresholds.
35:40 Alex: quick note about model routing: you can pin a route to a version or provide a fallback list. during heavy load automatic routing can downgrade to a compatible variant to keep latency SLOs.
37:12 Maya: any customers using the spend controls for experimental teams?
37:18 Samir: yes we've seen platform teams create dev routes with hard caps and per-team quotas to avoid surprise spend.
38:40 Priya: showing how to export a dashboard and attach it to a ticket - we often send dashboard exports and a short walkthrough video for pilots.
40:00 Ben: network questions - for Private, do you need peering?
40:05 Alex: Private deployments support VPC peering and on-prem; we'll share a network checklist. Dedicated can be run in cloud regions with VPC options.
41:50 Jordan: compliance pack - SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
41:55 Alex: we'll share our security pack and SCP. we provide SOC2 Type II, ISO docs, and third-party pen test summaries. addition: for air-gapped setups we support on-prem installs.
43:30 Maya: what's the success criteria for a pilot? we'd like clear cost-per-conversation and response latency under 300ms p95 for chat.
43:37 Alex: noted - we'll help instrument the pilot to measure cost per convo, token savings from KV caching, and end-to-end p95 latency.
45:10 Priya: last demo bit - role-based access, route-level permissioning, and audit logs. you can restrict who can change model bindings or rollout policies.
46:50 Sophie: can we get a sample dashboard that shows chargeback per product line?
46:55 Alex: yes i'll attach a sample CSV and dashboard export.
48:00 Maya: pricing - are there tiered discounts?
48:05 Alex: yes volume tiers and committed capacity discounts for Dedicated. we'll include examples in the pricing sheet.
49:40 Ben: ok next steps?
49:44 Alex: recap - Alex sends pricing and per-route cost example, Priya shares dashboard export + console walkthrough video, Cedar provisions trial account and provides pilot workloads & success criteria, schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2025-03-24.
50:30 Maya: thanks all, good walkthrough.
50:35 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with all docs.
50:40 [call ends]
